title: A Thin Crescent and a Patient Eye

content.question: What colour is the moon when it is only a thin crescent, and does the colour change with the thin light near the horizon?
content.method: I sat by the telescope on the lookout rock after dusk, when the sky was still pale, and kept my eye on the crescent for a long while without blinking more than I had to. I looked at it through the eyepiece, then past it at the dark sky beside it, then back again, and I did this three times so I would not trust a single look. I wrote down what I saw each time, and I left out what I hoped to see.
content.result: The crescent was not white. It was a pale, slightly warm yellow at the bright edge and a faint grey-blue where the dark part of the disc showed only by its outline. The colour seemed to shift with my own patience, which I did not expect, so I am less sure of the second and third looks than the first. I will need a clearer night and a thinner moon to be certain.
